title: Is .com still growing?
summary: After shrinking for 18 months in 2023 and 2024, .com hit an all-time high of 168.45 million domains in October 2026 (+6.8%). Zone data and Verisign filings.
body_markdown:
The[.com](https://instantdomainsearch.com/domain-extensions/com) extension is at an all-time high. On October 31, 2026, our daily count of the .com zone file reached **168.45 million** domains, up 10.75 million, or 6.8%, from a year earlier. That follows October changes of −2.5% in 2024 and +2.2% in 2025.


Two years ago, it looked like .com had peaked. Between July 2023 and December 2024, the zone shrank for 18 months in a row and shed nearly 5.8 million names from its 2022 high. Startups were buying .ai domains, and AI chat raised fair doubts about whether people would keep launching standalone websites at the old pace. Instead, .com hit bottom in early January 2025, passed its pandemic-era record in February 2026, and set a new month-end high in every month through October.


Verisign, which runs the .com registry, points to AI as part of that turnaround. Its[third-quarter 2026 report to the SEC](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1014473/000101447326000039/vrsn-20260930.htm) credits registrar marketing programs alongside “the evolution of AI tools used in content and website creation.” Over the same stretch, AI coding agents and website builders such as Replit and Lovable folded app creation, domain buying, and DNS setup into a single session. We looked at five years of daily .com zone files, Verisign’s filings, registrar integrations, and 133.1 million brand-new .com names to see how much of the rebound the evidence explains.


## Did .com peak in 2022?


During the pandemic boom, the .com zone climbed from 157.19 million domains on October 31, 2021, to a month-end peak of 159.56 million on April 30, 2022 (and a single-day high of 159.61 million on April 21, 2023). It held near 159 million for just over a year, then started sliding in July 2023. By October 31, 2024, the zone was down 2.5% from a year earlier at 154.35 million. It closed December 2024 at 153.86 million and touched its lowest single day on January 6, 2025, at 153.78 million.


That first week of 2025 was the bottom. In January 2025, .com grew again month over month, adding 205,186 net domains (+0.13%) to finish at 154.06 million. It has grown in all 22 months since, adding 14.6 million domains in total. On February 5, 2026, the daily zone file passed its pre-2026 record of 159.61 million, and across the first 10 months of 2026 it added an average of 975,000 net domains a month. In October 2026 alone, .com gained 1.45 million net domains, as we reported in our[November 2026 State of Domains report](https://instantdomainsearch.com/trends/november-2026) .


The year-over-year figure took five more months to turn because early 2025 was still measured against higher 2024 totals, after bottoming at −2.75% in September 2024. After 23 negative months in a row from July 2023 (−0.09%) through May 2025 (−0.66%), annual growth crossed back above zero in June 2025 at +0.08% (+129,089 domains over June 2024). It has sped up in all 17 months since, from +2.2% in October 2025 to +6.8% in October 2026.

Verisign’s quarterly registry count in the[Domain Name Industry Brief archive](https://www.dnib.com/listing/report) tells the same story on a slightly wider base. Verisign counts every registered .com name, including domains on hold or without nameservers, whereas the zone file counts domains set up to resolve in DNS, so we compare the two series rather than adding them together. Verisign’s .com base slipped from 161.6 million in the first quarter of 2023 to 156.3 million in the fourth quarter of 2024. It turned up again in the first quarter of 2025 (157.2 million) and beat its year-earlier level in the second quarter of 2025 (157.9 million against 157.6 million). On September 30, 2026, it hit a record 169.8 million (+6.5% in a year), beside 167 million in our zone file on the same day.


## Why registrations fell, and why they came back


Verisign’s SEC filings trace both halves of that curve. Through 2023 and 2024, the company blamed softer demand and stricter compliance rules among registrars in China, along with US retail registrars raising prices and pushing revenue per customer over new sign-ups. New registrations across .com and .net dropped to 9 million in the fourth quarter of 2023 and sat between 9.2 million and 9.5 million through 2024, while the combined renewal rate sagged to a final 72.2% in the third quarter of 2024.


Early 2025 brought back both new buyers and renewals. According to Verisign’s[third-quarter 2026 results](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1014473/000101447326000038/q32026earningsrelease.htm) and quarterly reports, gross new .com and .net registrations rose seven quarters in a row, from 10.1 million in the first quarter of 2025 to **13.1 million** in the third quarter of 2026. That third-quarter total was up 23.6% from a year earlier and set an all-time quarterly record for Verisign. Renewal rates climbed back to 75.4% in the third quarter of 2025 and 75.2% in the second quarter of 2026, before easing to a preliminary 74.3% in the third quarter of 2026 as 2025’s larger wave of first-year domains reached its first renewal.


In Item 2 of its[Form 10-Q for the third quarter of 2026](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1014473/000101447326000039/vrsn-20260930.htm) , Verisign writes that domain growth “has been positively impacted by continued registrar focus on customer acquisition and engagement with our marketing programs, as well as the evolution of AI tools used in content and website creation.” The filing puts registrar promotions and AI website builders side by side without giving either one a share.


Wholesale pricing also played a small timing role at the end of our window. Verisign raised the wholesale .com fee by 7%, from $10.26 to $10.97, on November 1, 2026, which likely pulled some registrations and multi-year renewals forward into late October’s 1.45 million net gain. Price timing alone does not explain the turnaround. Ahead of matching 7% wholesale increases on September 1, 2023, and September 1, 2024, the .com zone still lost 121,000 domains in August 2023 and 214,000 in August 2024. From January through September 2026, before the November fee change was near, .com was already adding 922,000 net domains a month.


## Buying a domain in Replit or Lovable


Some people bought a .com before building a website, left it on the registrar’s parking page, and let it expire a year later. Connecting an existing site to a domain often took several manual steps. Developers might need to add` A` ,` CNAME` , and` TXT` records, remove old` AAAA` records, obtain a TLS certificate, and update sign-in redirect URLs.


On July 16, 2025, Replit launched[Domain Purchasing on Replit](https://replit.com/blog/domain-purchasing-on-replit) . After Replit Agent builds an app, you search` .com` ,` .ai` , and other extensions inside the editor, buy a name, and go live in under a minute while Replit handles DNS records, HTTPS certificates, WHOIS privacy, and sign-in redirects.


Other AI builders wired registrar APIs straight into their editors over the next year. On August 4, 2026, registrar[Name.com announced embedded integrations](https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20260804252076/en/name.com-Partners-with-Leading-AI-Platforms-to-Bring-Domain-Access-to-Millions-of-Builders) with Lovable, Railway, Hercules, Sellfy, and Anything.com, noting that Lovable users registered thousands of domains in the first week alone. In[Lovable’s custom domain setup](https://docs.lovable.dev/features/custom-domain) , you buy a domain from the **Publish** dialog or ask Lovable in chat to find and register one. Lovable writes` A` records on its own nameservers without manual` TXT` verification, issues HTTPS certificates, sets up` www` , and redirects` your-app.lovable.app` to your domain.


Lovable’s checkout also runs an unintended pricing test on` .com` demand. Paid workspaces get one free first-year domain across 15 extensions, including` .app` ,` .dev` ,` .co` ,` .cloud` ,` .online` ,` .shop` ,` .store` , and` .tech` , and the dialog filters to those free choices by default. Because` .com` is left out of the free bundle, every` .com` bought inside Lovable comes from someone switching the filter to **All** and paying full price instead of taking a free extension.


## Chatbot speculation vs. product launches in 133 million new names


Zone files cannot see which tool built a website, but they do record every name people pick. We pulled all 133.1 million` .com` labels that entered our daily archive for the first time between November 1, 2021, and October 31, 2026, excluding any name seen since our archive began on May 31, 2016. Brand-new` .com` entries slipped from 25.7 million in 2022 to 25 million in 2023 and 24.1 million in 2024. Then they climbed to 26 million in 2025 and jumped 24.5% to **32.34 million** in 2026, adding 6.37 million more first-time` .com` names than the year before. In October 2026, 64.2% of` .com` zone entries were labels unseen since May 2016, 17.2% returned within 90 days, and 18.6% came back after more than 90 days out of the zone, which usually points to an expired domain registered again, as we found in our study of[domain age in zone files](https://instantdomainsearch.com/learn/guides/how-to-check-domain-age) .


The words inside those 133.1 million names show how different 2026 looks from the 2023 chatbot craze. After ChatGPT launched in late 2022, brand-new` .com` domains containing` gpt` jumped from 1,081 in 2022 to 82,154 in 2023. Even so, total first-time` .com` registrations fell by nearly 700,000 that year, and the overall` .com` zone shrank. Speculators rushing one buzzword could not move a 159-million-domain registry, and by 2026 new` gpt`` .com` names had fallen 88% to 9,457.


By 2025 and 2026, naming had moved toward software agents and shipped products. Brand-new` .com` domains containing` agent` sat near 18,500 a year in 2022 and 2023, climbed to 61,975 in 2025, and reached 88,810 in 2026, more than nine times` gpt` ’s count. Names starting or ending with` ai` quadrupled over five years from 128,875 to 528,878. More telling, brand-new` .com` domains using everyday software prefixes (` get` ,` try` ,` use` ,` build` ) or product suffixes (` app` ,` labs` ,` studio` ,` dev` ) grew 68% in a single year, from 758,906 in 2025 to 1,274,949 in 2026, rising from 2.9% to 3.9% of all first-time` .com` names (up from 1.4% in 2022).

Live web traffic shows the same scale gap between .com and newer extensions. Across the 952 public-zone extensions in our[November 2026 State of Domains](https://instantdomainsearch.com/trends/november-2026) dataset, .com holds 168.45 million of 259.9 million domains (64.8%) on October 31, 2026. Matched against the September 2026 Chrome UX Report list of the million most-visited web origins and September 30 zone counts (167 million .com domains), .com accounts for 319,439 distinct registered sites, or one busy site per 523` .com` domains. In that same dataset,[.app](https://instantdomainsearch.com/domain-extensions/app) has 3,353 sites (one per 502),[.ai](https://instantdomainsearch.com/domain-extensions/ai) has 2,286, and[.xyz](https://instantdomainsearch.com/domain-extensions/xyz) has 4,308 (one per 2,375` .xyz` domains).


## What we know about .com renewals


None of these numbers tell us how much of .com’s 10.75 million net gain belongs to AI. Over 94% of the 32.34 million brand-new` .com` domains from the past year use plain business, local, or personal words with no AI or software terms at all. When a bakery, a consultant, or a neighborhood club builds a website in Lovable or Replit and puts it on a` .com` , the zone file only records the domain name and its nameservers.


Large retail registrars offered introductory discounts again and took part in Verisign’s marketing rebate programs. Renewal rates rose about three percentage points from their 2024 low, and demand at registrars in China stopped falling. Only the registrars have the checkout data needed to distinguish purchases through AI builders from purchases driven by discounts.


The domains registered in 2026 come up for their first renewal in 2027. Owners renew first-year domains less often than older ones. Verisign reported a preliminary renewal rate of 74.3% across .com and .net in the third quarter of 2026, down from 75.4% a year earlier.


## How to check if a .com is available


With 32.34 million brand-new` .com` names taken in the past year alone, chatbots routinely suggest domains that someone already owns. Language models guess plausible names from training text rather than live zone data, and short, natural combinations in a 168.45-million-domain registry rarely sit open. Check availability instantly on[Instant Domain Search](https://instantdomainsearch.com/) as you brainstorm, or try variations in the[domain generator](https://instantdomainsearch.com/domain-generator) and[business name generator](https://instantdomainsearch.com/business-name-generator) before you build around a taken name. If you work inside Claude, ChatGPT, or Cursor, our free[Domain Search MCP](https://instantdomainsearch.com/mcp) and[ChatGPT plugin](https://instantdomainsearch.com/changelog/chatgpt-domain-search-plugin) let your assistant check candidates against our daily search index during the session, before you confirm final availability at a registrar’s checkout. When the` .com` you want is taken,[expired domains](https://instantdomainsearch.com/expired-domains) tracks recent drops and[domain appraisal](https://instantdomainsearch.com/domain-appraisal) estimates aftermarket value before you bid.


For how .com fits into all 411.6 million registered domains worldwide, read our guides on[why domain registrations are growing](https://instantdomainsearch.com/learn/guides/why-are-domain-registrations-growing) and[how many domains there are by extension](https://instantdomainsearch.com/learn/guides/how-many-domains-are-there) . We update monthly zone-file counts on[Domain name statistics](https://instantdomainsearch.com/domain-extensions/statistics) and in each monthly[State of Domains report](https://instantdomainsearch.com/trends) .


## Frequently asked questions


### How many .com domains are registered in 2026, and is that an all-time high?


On October 31, 2026, our daily count of the .com zone file reached an all-time month-end high of 168,454,855 domains, passing its pandemic-era peak of 159.56 million from April 2022 and growing by 10.75 million net (6.8%) in a year. Verisign’s broader quarterly registry count, which also includes domains on hold or without nameservers, likewise set a record of 169.8 million on September 30, 2026.


### When did .com start growing again?


In our daily .com zone archive, month-over-month growth resumed in January 2025 (+205,186 domains), right after hitting a daily low of 153.78 million on January 6, 2025. Year-over-year growth crossed back above zero in June 2025 (+0.08%) after 23 negative months in a row.


### Are startups replacing .com with .ai or .app?


Aggregate zone counts and website lists do not identify startups separately, so they cannot measure founder migration directly. Extensions such as .ai and .app are growing fast in percentage terms from smaller bases, while .com added 10.75 million net domains in the year to October 2026, more than the entire registered base of .ai and .app combined. In the September 2026 Chrome UX Report top-million list tracked in our November 2026 State of Domains dataset, .com also accounts for 319,439 distinct registered sites, compared with 3,353 on .app and 2,286 on .ai.


### How much of .com’s growth comes from AI tools?


Public data cannot isolate an exact share. Verisign’s third-quarter 2026 Form 10-Q credits AI content and website creation tools alongside registrar marketing programs, and integrations with builders such as Lovable and Replit show direct demand, but DNS zone files do not record how a domain’s website was built.
